The Scriptorium

On the hills surrounding the fields of battle, where skulls are crushed by mighty warhammers, warriors in plate clash with monsters from the cold north, and those who can command the winds of magic turn the living to ash.

The scribes watch, and do not look away.

Every deed is weighed.

Every death is recorded.

All of it is written in

This file needs your Supabase keys before it can connect.

Open this file in a text editor and find the CONFIG block near the top of the script. In Supabase, go to Project Settings → API and copy two things: your Project URL, and the public key (labelled "anon public", or "publishable" on newer projects). Paste them in, save, and reopen. Never use the "service_role" / "secret" key here.
Seeing this on a phone, or after opening the file directly (e.g. from Files, Messages or email) rather than a web link? The keys are probably already set — phone browsers block the page's connection code from running when it's opened as a local file rather than loaded from a proper https://… address. Ask whoever shared it with you for the hosted link instead.

                      New scenario

                      Start

                      Fills in a scenario from the online rules (tow.whfb.app): its map, set-up, deployment, first turn, game length, special rules and victory conditions. You can change anything afterwards, or leave this and start blank.

                      Fetching from the rules…

                      Battle size

                      Tick every size this scenario suits. Tables: 72"×48" is standard. At the smallest, 44"×30" up to 1,000 points, 60"×44" up to 3,000 and 90"×44" above that. Tick every size this scenario suits. Tables: 44"×30" for 400–600 points, 48"×36" above 600.

                      Deployment map

                      Set-up

                      With a generator, players roll each feature in Game view; with none, they pick it themselves. Roll 2D6 for each feature: one feature per 12" of the longest table edge (six on a 72" table). Each is 2–8" across. Roll the same result again and either place a second one, or swap the first for a larger one (8–12").

                      The winner of a roll-off places all the terrain, not within 12" of the centre. Then the loser picks D3 features and scatters each 2D6" (a Hit! leaves it where it is).

                        Awards

                        Best painted, best sportsman, best chronicler, or your own. Open voting and each player gets one secret vote per award; you see the totals. Or skip the vote and name a winner yourself. Winners show on their record and in standings, and everyone's told.

                        Battles in progress

                        Battles and requests still open in this campaign. You’re notified when one has been quiet for 3 hours; after 24 hours with no result sent, it closes itself. Closing one ends it for both players and records nothing.

                        Battle log

                        Fix a mis-entered result or points total, or remove a bad entry. Deleting a battle reverses any experience it granted. Add a battle nobody logged in Game view, including one with three or more players.

                              Campaign settings

                              • Name

                                What everyone sees the event called: on Play, in invites and in the player pack.

                              • Format

                                Campaign or tournament. Set once, when the event is made.

                              • Battles

                                Normal battles or Battle March, for the whole event, and the points limit for every army. Battle March is played at up to 750 points on a smaller table, with its own scenarios. Every scenario for the event is made for this.

                              • Dates

                                The day (or days) it runs. Leave either end blank if it’s not settled yet.

                              • Max players

                                How many can join with the code or link. Past that, players go on the waiting list. Organisers can always add players.

                              • Notes

                                Anything else players need to know, such as what to bring, food and parking. Shown on Play and in the player pack.

                              • Campaign points

                                The campaign points each result earns towards the campaign standings.

                              Scoring and ranking

                              • Scoring

                                How a battle’s result turns into tournament points.

                              • Byes

                                What a player gets for sitting out a round when there’s an odd number of players.

                              • Tiebreaks

                                When players are level on points, these decide who’s higher, in this order.

                              • Final ranking

                                Best General ranks on battles alone. Best Overall adds the soft scores, by their share.

                              Pairings and extras

                              • Pairings

                                How players are matched each round: round 1, which table the top players take, and who’s kept apart.

                              • Soft scores

                                Awards outside the battles themselves: painting, sportsmanship and favourite army.

                              • Comp

                                Rules to balance the armies, such as Square Based Comp’s tiers of extra points.

                              Leave either blank if it’s not settled yet.

                              Caps self-service joins (the join code or link). You and other organisers or platform admins can always be added past it.

                              Type of battle

                              Scoring

                              How close a battle must be to count as a draw. 0 means only an exact tie.

                              With an odd number of players, the lowest-ranked player who hasn’t had a bye gets it.

                              When players are level on points, these decide who’s higher, in this order. The official order puts total VP first; secondary-objective VP and Generals slain aren’t recorded per battle yet.

                                Keep apart

                                Always in round 1, and in later rounds where the scores allow. Players set their club in Account.

                                Awards outside the battles themselves. Turn on the ones you’re running; with Best Overall, each counts for its share of the overall score. Scores are entered on the day.

                                Comp

                                Each tier gets extra points to build with, and a kill point modifier: the VP an opponent scores against that army are multiplied by it. Players pick their tier on their Lists page; you can correct it in Players. No single character or unit may cost over 500 points (the Arachnarok excepted).

                                  Switches

                                  • Write pages in Campaign › Story first, then switch this on when you’re ready for players to read them.

                                  • Shared posts show photos and stories only, under “All campaigns”. Switching this off hides them from other campaigns straight away.

                                  • Unit XP, Veteran Abilities/Seasoned Commander rolls, and Battlefield Losses/Death & Dishonour. Turning this off just hides it — nothing already earned is lost, and it can be switched back on later.

                                  • Stops players changing their own alliance from Muster list. You can still reassign anyone from Membership.

                                  Audit trail

                                  Who changed what — membership, scenarios, phases, alliances, campaign settings, and any organiser edits to a player's battle log.

                                  Reading the muster roll…

                                  Danger zone

                                  While on: no new battles can be logged and no new players can join. Nothing is deleted or hidden — standings, rosters and narrative stay fully readable, and it can be switched back on at any time. Use this once a season wraps up.

                                  Players

                                  Every player on the platform and their rank — not just this campaign's roster.

                                  Campaigns

                                  Every campaign on Scriptorium, players’ drafts included. Anyone signed in can start one with the campaign builder and becomes its organiser.

                                  Opened to players straight away. You become its organiser; set the rest up in the admin tabs.

                                  Set once. A tournament has no narrative chapters and no alliances; its standings track the tournament, set up in Events › Tournaments once players have joined.

                                  Delete campaign

                                  Deletes whichever campaign is currently selected (the switcher in Account) — it and everything in it: rosters, battles, standings, narrative. Permanent, and superadmin-only. To wrap up a season without losing anything, use End campaign in Campaign › Settings instead.
